name: Linocut
summary: A relief print from a sheet of linoleum. The cut has smooth curves and no grain, and it prints flat colour.
how: Cut linoleum with V and U gouges; the sheet has no grain, so the cut curves freely.
Cut one block for each colour, and print from light to dark.
Print with opaque ink on thin paper, by hand with a spoon or on a hand press.
Keep each cut line at 1 mm to 3 mm, and each white gap at 1 mm or more.

origin.note: Artists of Die Brücke cut linoleum from about 1905. Vojtěch Preissig also made linoleum prints in 1911, in New York.

adoptions.via: Claude Flight and his group hold the first exhibition of British linocuts at the Redfern Gallery in London.
The Taller de Gráfica Popular opens in Mexico City and makes political prints from linoleum and wood blocks.
